decisions.reason: Proverbial “end in parting” is more natural than “in a parting” without changing meaning.
Splits the beat into cleaner English and drops the translated “I saw that it was.”
번쩍 is a flash; “gleaming” turns it into a steady shine.
“An exchange coupon” is the natural English for 교환 쿠폰; BASE is calqued.
Keeps restaurant coupons and 교환 쿠폰, and “trade” matches 바꾸다 better than restating “exchange.”
안 그래도 is the “anyway/too” already-needed beat; SOL drops it.
Keeps 아쉽 as shame and naturalizes the chopsticks line; SOL’s “only problem” is a meaning shift.
decisions.replacement: It was just a shame that I didn’t have a decent spear. I’d been using and discarding other weapons like disposable chopsticks from the very beginning.

decisions.reason: Singular 위기 and tighter “no urgent need” without adding meaning.
되게 갖고 싶었던 is “really wanted,” not unsupported “always wanted.”
쓱쓱 is a gentle stroke; SOL’s plain “ruffled” loses that softness.
“Meanwhile” is the natural rendering of 그사이.
The extra “be able to” is stiff; the prediction still carries 만날 수 있을 것이다.
The comma after “Then” is unnecessary pause not in 그럼 이만.
워낙…입구도 is the “even the entrance” emphasis, cleaner than “as well.”
“Speak with” is tighter spoken English for 이야기를 나눠 보다.
빙긋 is a pleasant smile; SOL drops that quality.
이라도 is “at least,” which BASE omits.
“One of his officers” already covers 휘하의 장수 without the extra phrase.
귀빈이시다 is unmarked; SOL’s plural “they/them” over-specifies.
그토록 염원하던 is desperate longing; SOL adds “finally,” drops that intensity, and uses unneeded past perfect.
Keeps 굳이 듣지 않아도 and 먼저; SOL’s “without being asked” and dropped “first” drift.
decisions.replacement: Even without hearing him say that, Cheongpung was someone I wanted to befriend first.

decisions.reason: “Besides” is the natural additive for 이기도 하고.
“Let me say this now” is the natural English for 말해 두는데.
다녀오기 is a round trip; BASE loses the return.
“Couldn’t have been gloomier” is the idiomatic match for 우울하기 짝이 없는.
퍼져 나가고 있을 is ongoing spread, not completed “had already spread.”
보며 is looking at them while clicking his tongue; SOL drops the look.
저, 정말이십니까 is a stammered “Really?”; BASE invents “going to do that.”
Keeps 앞으로는, 수밖에, and 몸집 as size; SOL’s “powerful” is a shift.
decisions.replacement: From now on, all they could do was grow as large as possible under the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

decisions.reason: 수고들 하고 is “do your best,” not a generic “take care”; 원단 is New Year’s Day.
decisions.replacement: “All right, then. Do your best, and I’ll see you on New Year’s Day.”

decisions.reason: “The express carriage” is the punchier, more natural taunt for this specific coach.
닫히기 무섭게 is the instant the door shut, not merely “as soon as.”
내부 as “inside” fits Taekyung’s voice; “interior” is a register bump.
따로 없네 identifies him as that primitive, not a simile with “like.”
“Asked with curious eyes” is translationese; the following line is still the question.
“Three or four” already means years old; the extra words are padding.
“Had his limits” is the idiomatic English for 한계가 있기 마련이다.
젖 정도야 나올 수 있지 is confident speculation; “might not” hedges it.
Spoken US English uses “nauseous” for 속이 메슥거리다.
쌍욕 is intensified swearing, not a literal “double curse.”
Spoken 역시 is “really is,” not the stiffer “As expected.”
입술에 뭘 발라 is lipstick, and SOL drops 그 사실.
Keeps 내시/고자 as attendant vs eunuch and 달린/안 달린 without SOL’s unsupported “still.”
decisions.replacement: I’d once heard that not every palace attendant was necessarily a eunuch. But there was no way to tell whether Hong Jin was equipped or not.

decisions.reason: “Y-Yes?” is the startled catch; doubled “Yes, yes?” over-reads 예, 예? as a stall.
Present “looking at” already carries 지금; “right now” is extra.
아 is “Ah,” and the rest is the same line.
절정 고수 is Peak, not Supreme Peak; 눈치 is reading the room, not generic perception.
decisions.replacement: He wasn’t a Murim martial artist, but his ability to read the situation was on the level of a Peak master. I quickly pulled my gaze away from Hong Jin’s lower body and changed the subject.

decisions.reason: 쭉 is “all the way”; SOL drops that stretch.
“That wasn’t the only reason” is more natural for 꼭 그런 것만은 아니에요.
Cheongpung’s “What’s” is the natural colloquial question.
“Among the top three in the military hierarchy” carries 품계로 without the clunkier “in terms of rank.”
“First is” matches the finger-counting, and “above us all” is cleaner for 모두의 위에.
“He’ll be retiring soon” is the natural spoken match for 은퇴를 앞둔.
그 모양인 인간 is “that kind of man,” not the flatter “person.”
Dropping “then” leaves the interrupted 차라리 line cleaner.
내가 뭐라고 is “who was I to,” not “why should I.”
해임도 마찬가지고 is more naturally “the same goes for dismissing him.”
그 이상의 욕심 is ambitions beyond that post, not generic “greater ambitions.”
뭐 이런 놈이 다 있어 is incredulous “what kind of person,” not “what the hell was wrong.”
Tighter, more natural English for TV politicians proclaiming innocence versus Hong Jin’s open admission.
뭐, 그렇죠 is “Well, yes,” not “Something like that.”
그거 알아요? is the “do you know what” setup; “something” sounds like a quiz.
물건이 없어 is the delayed euphemism “a thing”; “it” is too empty before the reveal.
고자라고 is the glossary identity “I’m a eunuch,” not a clinical “I’ve been castrated.”
갑자기 던질 줄이야 is “out of nowhere,” slightly more idiomatic than “suddenly.”
고자가 뭐예요 must follow the glossary reveal “eunuch,” not BASE’s “castrated.”
제발, 제발 is doubled “please, please”; SOL adds “just” and breaks the rhythm.
고추 is explicit and doubled; BASE censors, SOL drops the repetition.
decisions.replacement: *He’s saying he doesn’t have a dick—a dick!*

decisions.reason: “Without one / with one” is the natural countable follow-through, and dropping the second “people” is cleaner.
그……렇죠 is a mid-word break, which the em dash preserves better than a hyphen stammer.
눈치도 없이 is lack of tact, not a “sense of danger.”
The predicted line uses 고추; BASE’s “without one” censors the joke setup.
고자는 고추가 없어요 is the blunt glossary line, not a leftover “thing” euphemism.
Matches the predicted “without—” callback; BASE’s “who didn’t have” breaks it.
고자로 살고 있는 is “living as a eunuch,” which SOL flattens.
정말 죄송합니다 is Cheongpung’s “I’m truly sorry,” not formal “sincerest apologies.”
아직 달려 있잖아 is aimed at Taekyung; “Yours” is needed for the joke to land.
짬밥이 어디 가는 게 아니다 is experience that hasn’t gone anywhere, not “were no joke.”
Keeps 대수롭지 않게 as “nothing important”; SOL’s “nothing had happened” underplays it.
decisions.replacement: Hong Jin waved a hand as if to calm us down, then continued as though nothing important had happened.

decisions.reason: “I’ve never regretted my decision” is the natural spoken form of 후회한 적 없어요.
저도, 저도 is an em-dash break, not a hyphen stammer.
신의 is “a trust”; BASE’s “my loyalty” is an awkward collocation and SOL’s “someone’s” is extra.
decisions.replacement: “I’m not an upright man, but I’m not cowardly enough to betray a trust. If I were, I wouldn’t have continued serving His Highness all this time.”

decisions.reason: 흐릿한 시선 is a hazy gaze, not emotionally “distant.”
Fronting 오래전 gives cleaner English without changing the service or the order.
내관 is glossary “palace attendants,” not “eunuchs.”
귀양 아닌 귀양 is exile in all but name; “practically exile” beats “something like exile.”
알아차리다 is grasping what the light meant; “discern” is a register bump for this narrator.
마부 announcement register: “is in sight” for 보입니다, not a tourist “we can see.”
